name: Admit Road
tagline: College applications, timed and costed, for parents
about: Admit Road gives parents a month-by-month application timeline, builds a balanced college list around budget and fit, decodes financial-aid offers side by side, and preps campus visits and counsellor brag sheets.
persona: You are a former admissions officer turned family advisor: candid about odds and cost, allergic to prestige panic, and firm that the student owns the essays.

onboarding.title: The road to a good-fit yes
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where your student is and what you can afford.

tools.title: Build the timeline
tools.subtitle: From now to decision day

inputs.label: Aims
inputs.placeholder: engineering, Common App + 2 UC schools, needs aid

tools.prompt: Build an application timeline for the profile's student starting at '{start}', aims: {aims}, in the profile's system. Sections: a table (Month | Student does | Parent does | Deadline type), a checklist of documents and accounts to set up now (tests, transcripts, FAFSA/CSS or the local equivalent, recommendation requests), bullets on the difference between early and regular rounds, and a callout on the tasks parents must not do for the student.

tools.title: College list builder
tools.subtitle: Reach, match, likely — and affordable

inputs.label: Grades, tests, activities
inputs.placeholder: 3.7 GPA, 1350 SAT, robotics captain, part-time job

inputs.label: What they want
inputs.placeholder: mid-size, near a city, strong CS, not too far from home

tools.prompt: Build a balanced college list from: {stats}, wants: {wants}, priorities: {prefs}, within the profile's budget. Sections: a table of 12 schools (School | Tier: reach/match/likely | Est. net cost after typical aid | Why it fits | Watch-out), bullets on how the list is balanced and which to visit first, a callout on sticker price versus net price and merit-aid strategy, and a kv of next actions per tier.

tools.title: Campus visit kit
tools.subtitle: What to ask, what to notice
tools.prompt: Prepare a {format} visit to {school} for the profile's student. Sections: a checklist of what to observe (the dining hall at noon, the library on a weeknight, the notice boards), bullets of 8 questions the student asks (not the parent) with the answer to hope for, a table (Question for the financial-aid office | Why it matters), and a quote with a 3-line debrief prompt for the car ride home.

tools.title: Decode aid offers
tools.subtitle: Compare real net cost

inputs.label: Paste the offers
inputs.placeholder: School A: COA 62k, grant 30k, loan 5.5k, work-study 2k. School B: …

tools.prompt: Decode and compare: {offers}. Sections: a table (School | Cost of attendance | Gift aid | Loans | Work-study | True net cost | 4-year estimate), a callout on which lines are free money versus debt and any one-year-only awards, bullets on how to appeal for more aid and what evidence works, and a quote with a short, polite appeal email the family can send.

tools.title: Brag sheet
tools.subtitle: For counsellor & recommenders

inputs.label: Stories, achievements, growth
inputs.placeholder: started robotics club, cared for grandma, improved chem from C to A

tools.prompt: Turn {notes} into a parent brag sheet for the counsellor and recommenders of the profile's student. Sections: a kv (three words that describe them with an anecdote each, a challenge overcome, what they do when nobody's watching, growth since Grade 9), bullets of concrete achievements with numbers, a quote with a 150-word paragraph a counsellor could adapt, and a callout on what recommenders don't want to read.

disclaimer: Cost and aid figures are estimates, not financial advice; verify with each institution's official net-price calculator and aid office.
